verdicts.question: Under the HOWM Rules 2016 as amended to 2026 (Rule 9 utilisation, CPCB SOPs, Schedules I to IV, and any 2024-26 amendment defining 'by-product' or 'end of waste'), which of the founder's industrial by-product rows may be listed and sold on an ordinary marketplace by their generator, and which may move only to an authorised recycler, co-processor or TSDF with a Form 10 manifest and SPCB authorisation? Cite the schedule entry or SOP per family. What did the Fly Ash Notification (2021) and the 2024 amendments on utilisation change?
verdicts.problems: Verification limit first: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before the sceptic pass and page fetches are refused, so none of the 24 cited sources could be re-found by snippet; the checks below rest on the repo's earlier dated research (docs/plan/research/answers/epr-portals, swm-2026, risk-guards, materials) and on the rule text as I recall it, and are marked as such. (1) 'Schedule I (128 wastes from 38 processes)': Schedule I of the 2016 Rules lists 36 processes (1 petrochemical ... 36 hazardous-waste treatment processes); '38' and '128' are unsupported. (2) Entry numbers are misplaced: ETP sludge is not 'entry 9.2' (process 9 is secondary production of lead); the generic entry is 34.3 'chemical sludge from waste water treatment' under process 34 (purification processes for air and water); spent solvents sit at 20.2 (process 20, production and/or industrial use of solvents) and 35.2 (process 35, purification of organic compounds/solvents); spent catalyst at 1.6 (petrochemicals) and 18.1 (fertilisers); aluminium 11.5 reads 'wastes from treatment of salt slags and black drosses', so dross itself is covered by the process-11 entries only as those residues. None of these is confirmed by a snippet either way; the answer's own 'not confirmed' flags were right, but the 9.2 attribution is wrong. (3) 'Mill scale is listed only in Schedule III Part B': Schedule IV (recyclable other wastes requiring registration) contains 'copper oxide mill scale' alongside brass dross, copper dross, zinc dross (hot-dip galvaniser slab and bottom dross), zinc ash/skimmings, spent metal catalysts containing Cu/Zn/Ni/Co, lead-acid batteries and used/waste oil; so zinc, brass and copper dross recyclers are Schedule IV registrants, not 'Schedule I' cases, and the mill-scale statement is at best incomplete. (4) Fly ash: the answer admits the 100%/80%/300 km/Rs 1,000 per tonne figures come from the draft and a Dec 2021 critique, not the final S.O. 5481(E) of 31 Dec 2021; that is an open item, not a settled figure. (5) C&D concrete: the answer cites 'the C&D rules and local-body permits' without the operative instrument, the Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules 2025 (G.S.R. 219(E), April 2025), in force 1 Apr 2026 with producer and recycler registration on cdwm.cpcb.gov.in (repo research, 29 Sep 2026); the pilot's earlier decision was to leave C&D out of scope. (6) 'Delhi High Court ruled in April 2026 that FSSAI cannot regulate animal feed': not confirmed by any snippet or repo record; treat as unverified. (7) Molasses is listed as 'free to sell', but molasses is an excise-controlled commodity in Karnataka (state molasses rules govern its sale and movement for distillery use); this needs counsel before it goes on an open list. (8) The '2019 CPCB by-product framework', '23 Sep 2019' circulation and 'eight guiding factors' are plausible but unconfirmed. (9) No newer 2026 instrument redefining 'by-product' was found in the repo either; but the answer misses two 2026 instruments that touch these rows: the SWM Rules 2026 (S.O. 388(E), 27 Jan 2026, in force 1 Apr 2026: sorting entities register with the local body under rule 9, bulk generators register with CPCB) and the C&D Rules 2025 above. (10) Fit with the refined chain: the answer's 'HAZARDOUS list, no trade at all' conflicts with the founder's model, which routes aluminium dross to a dross mill (KSPCB Orange 1337) and used oil to re-refiners (1339/1340) as pre-processors, and it does not say where the SPCB by-product acceptance attaches (to a generator+material pair, not to a lot) nor that L3 prices for hazardous residues are often negative (the generator pays the TSDF), which the five-level price model must allow.
verdicts.correction: Keep the legal test as stated (Schedule I process/waste entry or a Schedule II concentration limit makes it hazardous waste; Rule 9(1) requires SPCB authorisation on CPCB SOPs for any utilisation; every movement carries the Form 10 manifest under rule 19(1)), but fix the entries and the split. Schedule I has 36 processes, not 38. Family to entry: spent solvents 20.2 and 35.2 (contaminated solvents 20.1/35.1, distillation residues 20.3/35.3); spent catalysts 1.6 (petrochemicals) and 18.1 (fertilisers); paint sludge and residues 21.1; ETP sludge 34.3 (chemical sludge from waste water treatment) plus the process-specific sludge entries; aluminium: process 11 (11.5 wastes from treatment of salt slags and black drosses; dross itself moves under the CPCB aluminium-dross SOP); zinc/brass/copper dross, zinc ash/skimmings, copper oxide mill scale, spent Cu/Zn/Ni/Co catalysts, lead-acid batteries and used oil are Schedule IV recyclables whose buyers must hold SPCB registration/authorisation. Three lists, not two. OPEN (ordinary GST invoice, no manifest): bagasse, press mud, rice husk and bran, sawdust, textile cuttings, fly and bottom ash, steel slag and ferrous mill scale, tyre steel, whey, fish offal, bones, hides; PET caps and labels only to a PWM-registered processor; C&D concrete only to a processor registered under the C&D Rules 2025 (in force 1 Apr 2026, cdwm.cpcb.gov.in), which the pilot had already scoped out; molasses is excise-controlled in Karnataka, so hold it until counsel confirms the permit route. REGISTERED-BUYER (Schedule IV): zinc, brass and copper dross and skimmings, copper oxide mill scale, used oil (Chapter VII EPR from 1 Apr 2024, G.S.R. 677(E)), lead-acid batteries; from 1 Apr 2026 the non-ferrous EPR chapter (G.S.R. 438(E), 1 Jul 2025) adds CPCB registration, but its portal and target rules are not working yet (Business Standard, 20 Sep 2026), so the SPCB authorisation number is the usable gate. HAZARDOUS-ONLY (Schedule I, SPCB-authorised recycler, co-processor or TSDF, Form 10): spent solvents, spent catalysts, paint sludge, ETP sludge, aluminium dross and salt slag, and foundry sand or de-inking sludge unless a Schedule II test report and the SPCB's by-product acceptance (CPCB by-product framework, 2019) are on file for that generator and material. Fly ash: the 2021 notification's 100% utilisation over a three-year cycle and the compensation figure remain an open item until the final S.O. 5481(E) text of 31 Dec 2021 is read. 2024-26: G.S.R. 177(E) (12 Mar 2024) changed tyre and used-oil EPR; G.S.R. 438(E) (1 Jul 2025, from 1 Apr 2026) added non-ferrous EPR; no amendment redefining 'by-product' was found. Model changes: store the routing flag on the material row (the founder's CSV 'Flag' column already carries 'Hazardous', 'EPR stream', 'Co-processing route', 'By-product logistics'); attach the SPCB by-product acceptance to the generator+material pair; let residual-waste output lots of a processing record carry the Schedule I entry and Form 10 fields; and allow a negative L3 price (disposal fee) for hazardous residues.

verdicts.question: What obligations fall on a platform that lists such materials: does hosting a listing for a Schedule I waste make Luma.Green an 'operator of a facility', a 'dealer' or otherwise liable under the HOWM Rules, the E-Waste Rules 2022 or the Battery Waste Management Rules 2022, and how do Recykal, Scrapcart, MetalMandi, Karo Sambhav and MSTC's e-auction handle it? Recommend the buyer-gate rules per material family.
verdicts.problems: Same verification limit: no WebSearch budget remained and fetches are refused, so the 15 cited sources could not be re-found by snippet; checks rest on repo research dated up to 29 Sep 2026 and on the rule text as I recall it. What stands: the HOWM duties sit on the occupier, transporter and operator of a disposal facility and there is no marketplace or 'dealer' category; the E-Waste Rules 2022 clause 'no entity shall carry out any business without registration and also shall not deal with any unregistered entity' and the informal-seller receipt requirement match the CPCB FAQ of 23 Jan 2024 held in the repo; used-oil collection is limited to registered collection agents from 1 Apr 2024 (repo, epr-portals). What does not: (1) 'abettor under s.15 of the Environment (Protection) Act': s.15 is the penalty section, not an abetment provision, and since the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2023 took effect for the EPA (1 Apr 2024) s.15 contraventions are civil penalties set by an adjudicating officer, not prosecution; the exposure to describe is a penalty notice plus SPCB direction, and the Jan Vishwas Act 2026 (in force for other statutes from 1 May 2026, repo) continued that decriminalisation, so the framing is out of date. (2) Gate B 'non-ferrous dross and scrap from 1 Apr 2026 only to a registered non-ferrous recycler' is not enforceable today: the repo's 20 Sep 2026 Business Standard record says the non-ferrous EPR portal and target rules have gaps, nobody can currently register and the first half-yearly returns fall due 31 Oct 2026 with a nine-month relaxation power under Rule 50(4); the usable gate is the buyer's SPCB HOWM authorisation or Schedule IV registration. (3) Gate C 'no trade' for aluminium, zinc and copper dross conflicts with the founder's refined chain, which routes dross to a dross mill (KSPCB Orange 1337) as a pre-processor, and with Schedule IV, under which zinc, brass and copper dross are registrable recyclables, not Schedule I wastes; only aluminium salt slag and black-dross residues belong in Gate C. (4) The gates omit C&D concrete (C&D Rules 2025, registration on cdwm.cpcb.gov.in from 1 Apr 2026) and the SWM Rules 2026 duty that sorting entities register with the local body, both of which bear on who may buy from a yard. (5) The platform-practice claims are thin: for MetalMandi the repo already holds a FAQ (26 Mar 2026) showing KYC (Aadhaar/PAN) plus GST for dealers and that Attero, a registered recycler, was the sole buyer until third-party buyers were opened in April 2026 (Financial Express, 13 Apr 2026), which answers the gating question the answer left open; MSTC's notarised-certificate and validity-date practice, the NGT 2021 spent-catalyst order and the 'refurbisher under own brand becomes a producer' reading are plausible but not confirmed by any snippet. (6) The answer never states the IT Act s.79 / IT Rules 2021 intermediary position for a listing-only platform, which is the actual legal shelter, and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Amendment Rules 2026 (repo, 14 Sep 2026) for any consumer-facing listing.
verdicts.correction: On the text of the HOWM Rules a listing-only platform that takes no title or custody, runs no site and moves no money is not an occupier, transporter or operator of a disposal facility, and there is no 'dealer' category; the residual exposure is a civil penalty under s.15 EPA (decriminalised by the Jan Vishwas Act 2023, in force for the EPA from 1 Apr 2024, with adjudicating officers under the 2024 inquiry-and-penalty rules) and SPCB directions, plus loss of IT Act s.79 safe harbour if the platform fails the IT Rules 2021 due-diligence duties, so publish terms that make the generator the occupier, keep the platform on the data side and remove a listing on notice. E-waste (Rules 2022, in force 1 Apr 2023): no entity may deal with an unregistered entity and recyclers must upload seller receipts (CPCB FAQ, 23 Jan 2024); batteries (BWM Rules 2022, amended G.S.R. 190(E), 14 Mar 2024): recyclers and refurbishers register on the CPCB portal and CPCB's 11 Jun 2026 classification of waste-battery collection centres applies before any battery lot is listed; used oil: registered collection agents and re-refiners only since 1 Apr 2024; non-ferrous scrap: G.S.R. 438(E) in force 1 Apr 2026 but the portal is not issuing registrations, so use the buyer's SPCB authorisation until it does. Platforms: MSTC admits only CPCB/SPCB-registered recyclers to hazardous lots; Recykal.Market requires GST certificate, PAN and bank KYC and routes EPR lots to CPCB-authorised recyclers; MetalMandi requires KYC plus GST and until April 2026 sold everything to Attero itself, a registered recycler; Scrapcart and Karo Sambhav are unconfirmed. Gates: Gate A open (admin-verified GSTIN): bagasse, press mud, husk, bran, sawdust, textile cuttings, fly and bottom ash, steel slag, ferrous mill scale, tyre steel, whey, fish offal, bones, hides (molasses held for excise counsel). Gate B registered-for-the-stream (number, PDF, expiry on the buyer profile, admin-checked, listing hidden from others): PET caps/labels and all plastic lots to PWM-registered processors; e-waste to CPCB-registered recyclers or refurbishers; batteries to CPCB/KSPCB-registered recyclers or refurbishers; used oil to registered collection agents or re-refiners; zinc, brass and copper dross, skimmings and copper oxide mill scale to buyers holding SPCB HOWM authorisation (Schedule IV), switching to the CPCB non-ferrous registration when the portal issues it; C&D concrete to processors registered under the C&D Rules 2025 (or keep C&D out of the pilot as already decided). Gate C request-only, no price, bidding, escrow or Saathi pickup: spent solvents, spent catalysts, paint sludge, ETP sludge, aluminium salt slag and black-dross residues, and foundry sand or de-inking sludge without a Schedule II test report and SPCB by-product acceptance; capture the Form 10 fields and show KSPCB-authorised recyclers, co-processors and TSDFs. Model changes: the gate is a property of the material row and its state (a Gate C residual-waste lot from a processing record can never be promoted to Gate A by relabelling), the by-product acceptance attaches to the generator+material pair, and L3 prices for Gate C lots may be negative. Counsel to confirm the occupier/operator reading, the s.79 position and the Gate B treatment of dross before 13 Oct 2026.
